trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,7); going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Cell (7,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes up.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going down would force the line onto number 6 before its turn; going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes left.
Going left would cut off the bottom-left corner (8 cells). So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both cell (5,1) and number 7 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Cell (6,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
Going down would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Cell (1,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would cut off the left side (4 cells); going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going up would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going right would strand number 12: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would wall in number 16, the last number. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
